body.p: REMARKS

Claims 1-19 are pending. Claim 19 is new. Claims 11-18 are withdrawn. In the following sections of this Response, the election requirement set forth in the September 20, 2024 communication is addressed. The election requirement is respectfully traversed, and detailed arguments are set forth herein. The election requirement is respectfully traversed, and detailed arguments are set forth herein.
The Office Action requires applicant to elect a single species for

prosecution on the merits to which the claims shall be restricted if no generic claims are finally held to be allowable. It was advised that the reply must include an election of a single species for prosecution on the merits. In particular, the following alleged species were identified as:
I. Group A - FIGS. 2-10 detailing a leverage reducing system for energy absorption.
II. Group B - FIGS. 13-17 detailing a constant angle suspension mechanism.

Applicant provisionally elects to pursue Group A (FIGS. 2-10). Claims 1-10 and 19 are identified as readable on the elected group. This election is made with traverse. Although species A has been elected, if species A is found allowable, applicant respectfully requests that Species B be considered.

35 U.S.C. §121 specifically states, "If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in one application, the Director may require the application to be restricted to one of the inventions." (Emphasis added.) Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner may have applied the wrong test. Specifically, the Examiner states that the "species are independent or distinct...." (Emphasis added.) While the Examiner states that the species describe "two separate types of landing gear" and that they are "not obvious variants of each other," applicant respectfully requests clarification of how this makes the two species "independent" AND how this makes the two species "distinct." Applicant respectfully points out that aircraft can have
both types of landing gear. As noted in M.P.E.P. §806.04(f), "claims to be restricted to different species must recite the mutually exclusive characteristics of such species." (Emphasis added.)
New claim 19 includes the elements of both claims 1 and claim 11.

Accordingly, since the examination of claim 19 would include all the elements of claim 11, applicant respectfully submits that it would not be a serious burden on the Examiner to examine all the claims together if restriction is not required.

It is applicant's understanding that the above species election is being made to aid the Examiner in conducting a search and examination of the claimed subject matter, and is not to be construed as limiting the scope of applicant's claims. It is applicant's understanding also that, if the elected subject matter is found to be allowable over the prior art, the search and examination will be expanded to cover other species until it includes the full scope of the generic claims of the invention.
Applicant specifically requests reconsideration of this requirement based on the traversal and arguments set forth above.
Applicant respectfully requests an acknowledgement that the right to petition the Commissioner to review the requirement has been preserved.
Applicant specifically reserves the right to file divisional applications,
continuation applications, or other types of applications to pursue the subject matter of the claims that have been withdrawn.

Applicant specifically reserves the right to have claims considered that are directed to non-elected species upon allowance of a generic claim. Further, applicant specifically reserves the right to file divisional applications, continuation applications, or other types of applications to pursue the subject matter of withdrawn claims.
Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reexamine the application, allow the claims, and promptly pass the application on to issue.
